evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep never delivered the time-boxed framing ('this will take 10–15 minutes, you can walk away with a quote you can depend on') before probing. Went directly into logistics after confirming the call was about the September 30th request.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asked: 'Besides pricing, do you have any questions or concerns you would like answered on this call?' — asked before logistics probing began. Customer answered no initial concerns but volunteered context about the move itself.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer did not raise any concerns in Section 2. Customer explained the situation (daughter-in-law and grandchildren's items in garage) but did not express concerns that would require follow-up.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns were raised, so no reflection was needed.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep covered property type (garage / second floor destination), number of items (full-size bed, metal bunk beds, small couches, boxes), bulky items detail, fragility check, assembly needs, destination address, floor/stair access, walking distance (initially 50 feet, customer corrected to ~200 feet max), boxes present, and box count estimate (15–25 range).
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Rep did not offer packing services. Rep discussed assembly help for the bunk bed but never asked 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep asked: 'A typical box count for a move this size is about fifteen to 25 boxes. Do you feel like you fall within that range?' — customer confirmed yes.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provided: '$208 for two movers, 126 foot box truck' for the value day (September 30th), plus trip fee ($140), plus hourly ranges ($670 for 2.5 hours, $878 for 3.5 hours). Personalized by noting 'you would easily fall within that two and a half, three and a half hour range' and explaining prep efficiency ('how well prepared you are when we get there... less time we take less money you spend').
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep disclosed: trip fee ($140), no deposit required, no change charges, two and a half hour minimum, fifteen minute increments, all-inclusive hourly rate (fuel, trucks, taxes, insurance, pads, tools, disassembly/reassembly). Rep stated 'no hidden fees, no credit card fees, no stairwell fees' and 'the time starts as soon as we get on site and open the contract.' Rep did not explicitly frame as 'not a guess' or reiterate the 2.5-hour minimum with the commitment language from the script.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or any version of it. Rep moved directly from pricing explanation into availability windows without a closing check or pause.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep stated: 'We have our on time guarantee if you can't make it in the time window that we arrange, you mainly start to discounting money of your final bill.' The phrasing is slightly unclear ('you mainly start to discounting money') but the core concept (discount if late) is present. Discount terms are conveyed but with imprecise wording.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep stated: 'We do have a no worries damage coverage. Which is our free evaluation coverage included in the hourly rate. We're talking about provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages that is on top of the 60¢ man Texas mandated one that we have that were all required to have to which covers nothing. Basically.' Rep covered $2,000 limit, included in hourly rate (no add-on), and no fine print framing (contrast with Texas minimum). No explicit mention of 'no deductible,' but the 'included in the hourly rate' + contrast with the Texas mandate implies coverage is straightforward.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep did not ask a version of 'Does that put those to rest?' or confirm that the Two Promises section resolved the customer's concerns. Rep transitioned directly to availability windows.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep never asked a final concerns check. Rep went directly to offering time windows: 'I do have two arrival times available on that date. I have the 8:30 AM to 9:00 AM arrival or I have the 12:30 AM to 2:30 PM arrival time.' No version of 'What's still concerning you?' or genuine final-check question was asked.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Rep never asked 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or a version of that catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any equivalent ask for the business. Customer volunteered to 'let me get with my wife and daughter-in-law and see what date what time works better for them and... I will call you back,' and rep accepted that without asking for the commitment directly.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Rep stated: 'There is no deposit required to get on our schedule. So no risk and securing your spot and there's no change charges or fees to cancel or change the date if need[ed].' This covers the no-deposit and flexibility aspect. No explicit 'rate lock' language, but the commitment and no-change language is present.

top_strength: Brianne gathered comprehensive logistics details efficiently—property type, bulky items, fragility, assembly needs, destination specifics, box count, and walking distance—and delivered a full pricing breakdown with all-inclusive rate transparency and trip fee disclosure upfront, making the estimate feel concrete and dependable.
coaching_note: This call skipped the critical Section 1 quid pro quo (the 10–15 minute time-box and quote promise framing), never asked for the business in Section 7, and missed both the final concerns check and catch-all in Section 6—the customer left without a yes or commitment, leaving money and close rate on the table.
